subtitle: "Check the habits that make terminal work understandable and repeatable."

Choose an answer before opening its feedback. If a question is uncertain, try its command in the practice workspace, then return to the [key points](key-points.html).

::: {.checkpoint title="Which layer interprets a command?"}
When you enter `ls data/raw` in the course's terminal, what interprets the command line?

- [x] Bash, the shell

  Bash interprets the command and arguments, then invokes the relevant command.
- [ ] The terminal window alone

  The terminal provides the input/output interface; it can host different shells.
- [ ] The sample sheet

  The sample sheet is input data, not a command interpreter.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="Where does a relative path begin?"}
You run `python scripts/count_samples.py data/raw/samples.tsv` from the project root. Where does this example's input path begin?

- [x] At the current working directory

  The program opens the relative path from its working directory, inherited from the shell.
- [ ] Inside `scripts/`, because that contains the program

  A program's location does not automatically change its working directory.
- [ ] Always at the filesystem root `/`

  A path starting with `/` is absolute; this one is relative.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="A path from results"}
You are inside `mm-linux-lab/results`. Which path reaches the raw sample sheet?

- [x] `../data/raw/samples.tsv`

  `..` returns to the project root, from which `data/raw/` is accessible.
- [ ] `data/raw/samples.tsv`

  That looks for a `data` directory inside `results`.
- [ ] `/data/raw/samples.tsv`

  The leading slash starts at the filesystem root, not at your project.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="A filename with spaces"}
Which command passes a path containing a space as one argument?

- [x] `head -n 2 "scratch/sample notes.tsv"`

  Quotes keep the complete path together.
- [ ] `head -n 2 scratch/sample notes.tsv`

  The space separates two arguments, neither of which is the intended complete path.
- [ ] `head -n 2 scratch/sample*notes.tsv` is always equivalent

  A glob may match additional filenames or nothing; exact quoting expresses the intended file.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="How many samples?"}
The fixture has a header, six records, no blank lines and a newline after every line. What does `wc -l` report?

- [x] Seven lines

  The header contributes one newline in addition to the six records.
- [ ] Six lines

  That is the number of sample records, not the number of lines including the header.
- [ ] The number of columns

  The `-l` option counts newline characters, not fields.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="Protect the input"}
You want to practise renaming and deleting files. Which workflow best preserves the original sample sheet?

- [x] Copy it into `scratch/` and operate on that exact copy

  The practice operations have an explicit disposable target, while raw input stays separate.
- [ ] Rename the raw input and try to remember its old name

  That changes a shared input path and can break other commands.
- [ ] Remove every matching `*.tsv` file after the exercise

  A broad pattern can include raw inputs or other valuable files.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="Which interpreter?"}
After activating an environment, which command helps confirm how Bash resolves `python`?

- [x] `command -v python`

  It shows the command Bash resolves; `python --version` adds its version.
- [ ] `pwd`

  This shows the working directory, not the interpreter selected through PATH.
- [ ] `ls data/raw`

  This lists inputs and says nothing about Python resolution.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="An empty output file"}
A script fails after its output was redirected with `> results/report.tsv`. Why might the report file still exist?

- [x] Bash can create or truncate the file before the program executes

  Check exit status, diagnostics and output validity before using it.
- [ ] An existing file proves the script completed successfully

  File creation and a complete successful calculation are different events.
- [ ] Standard error automatically repairs standard output

  Standard error is a diagnostic stream; it does not repair results.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="Save the right status"}
How should you preserve the exit status of a Python command before printing other messages?

- [x] Assign `status=$?` immediately after the Python command

  Later commands replace `$?`, while the saved variable preserves the value you need.
- [ ] Print several messages, then read `$?`

  That reads the exit status of the last message-printing command.
- [ ] Assume an empty diagnostic log always means scientific correctness

  A silent program can still use the wrong data or make invalid assumptions.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="A background job"}
What does `sleep 30 &` do in an interactive Bash terminal?

- [x] Starts a background process and returns the prompt

  `jobs` can show the shell's job and `$!` captures its PID.
- [ ] Submits a durable job to the research cluster scheduler

  Backgrounding alone is not cluster scheduling and does not guarantee survival after a disconnect.
- [ ] Stops every process after 30 seconds

  `sleep` waits; it does not terminate other programs.
:::
